To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Transformer-XL language modeling performance drops off over time; (ii) model performance can be improved by continually updating the model with new data; and (iii) we release our benchmarks to facilitate language modeling research that takes temporal dynamics and continual learning into account

(i) current static language models do not generalize to future utterances beyond their training period; and (ii) this problem can be mitigated with adaptive language models that continually update themselves with new information

1) Transformer-XL language model performance degrades over time when evaluated on future utterances from out-of-training periods; 2) this degradation can be alleviated by continually updating model knowledge with new information, as demonstrated by a simple streaming training approach that updates models with new data from each time step; 3) the performance of the best performing streaming model is comparable to the performance of the static model, and is better than that of a static model trained on a larger dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with

assessing the ability of neural language models to learn to generalize over time, and we find that they do not do this very well.
